questions.question: A rectangle is 3 squares long and 2 squares high. Describe its enlargement with every side 3 times as long.
questions.expected_answer: Multiply every side by 3. The enlargement is 9 squares long and 6 squares high, and its angles are still right angles.

questions.question: Explain why a 6 by 3 rectangle is not an enlargement of a 3 by 2 rectangle.
questions.expected_answer: The long side was multiplied by 2, but the short side was multiplied by only 1 and a half. In an enlargement every side must be multiplied by the same number, so this shape has been stretched.

questions.question: The sides of a 3 by 2 rectangle are doubled. How does the number of squares inside change?
questions.expected_answer: It grows from 6 squares to 24 squares. Doubling the sides doubles both the length and the width, so the inside becomes 4 times as big.
